330 SmoothieBox exterior wiring studies: each primary SVG shows the four-sided SmoothieBox exterior case with numbered screw contacts and source-scoped machine interface cards alongside it. A dotted violet path, where shown, runs from the exact highlighted exterior screw to a machine contact circle as a function-only GUESS; it does not prove continuity or a fitted cable. OPEN means this study selects no SmoothieBox route, not that a source pin is NC or unused. Click once for fullscreen, then again to zoom and drag to pan. Earlier diagrams stay in closed disclosures.

Read the exterior case and adjacent machine cards

The case drawing shows outside connectors on all four sides, with machine interface cards alongside. A highlighted screw is a proposed controller endpoint; a dotted violet line reaches a source-marked machine contact circle only where a function match is guessed. The electrical interface and installed cable remain unverified. OPEN marks no SmoothieBox route selected here; it does not make a source contact NC or unused. Card headings distinguish reported fitted or used, listed, historical, planned, and unresolved hardware; these source states do not establish pin-level wiring. Source-local paths document only their cited machine design. Motor windings, power, laser and spindle loads require qualified circuits.

A V2 Core production terminal contract and several extension circuits are unresolved. In particular, the 0–10 V spindle adapter is a blocked concept. Match every source against the installed revision, connector view, voltage, return path and safety circuit before making wiring or a sticker.

The published 440 path runs through DB25 J4/J10 and IDC26 to the cabinet board/MX3660. Pin 10 is a limit/door input and pin 15 is E-stop reset; neither proves the cabinet's safety circuit. Pins 18–25 and electrical ratings remain unresolved. Tormach 440 electrical schematic index.

Separate cabinet article identifies MX3660 PN33374, DB25 ribbon PN35721, 24 V and 48 V supplies. Interface reading

Signal domains: Motion control or motor phases, limits/probe, spindle and safety where fitted. Controller family: Sherline 8760 driver box.

What is still missing

8760-specific; motor DIN separate. Confirm actual hardware, contact orientation, electrical levels, wire identity, and safety function before a V2-Core label. Do not apply the 67126 color map to an unidentified motor. Driver-board H3 removes power immediately but is not a certified E-stop.

Sherline 8760 DB25 high is >2 V and low <0.5 V; the active-low step pulse is at least 22 μs. The driver-box supply is 24 V DC / 4 A and is not the DB25 logic rating. DIN motor wiring is a separate winding-output domain. 8760 product specification.

Documented evidence · unresolved wiring

Documented: Sherline 8760 driver box, product wiring section; Sherline high-torque stepper specification, dated 2020-03-10, PDF pp. 1–2, P/N 67126 / 23Y-240D-LW5-01 only. 8760 DB25 logic inputs: X direction/step 2/3, Y 4/5, Z 6/7, A 8/9, ground 18–25; active-low step at least 22 µs, high >2 V, low <0.5 V. 5-pin DIN motor output male connector external view: 1 orange, 2 blue, 3 brown+green center taps, 4 yellow, 5 red. Unresolved: axis installed motor identity, connector mating view, 8760 version and safety integration. Keep phase output separate from DB25 step/dir.

Documented evidence · unresolved wiring

Documented: Homann Designs TurboTaig 2.2 manual, v2.2, PDF p. 6 DB25 J9/J10 alternatives and connector descriptions. The published connector table covers J1/J2/J29/J30 limits, J3 emergency, J4 enable, J5 selector; its DB25 pin 14 wording is internally conflicting and should be checked against manual circuit before use. This is an aftermarket/add-on TurboTaig, not the stock Taig DSLS control. Unresolved: installed J9 versus J10 route, contact view, revision and verified voltage/safety.

Supplemental contact map · 2026-09-27

The page 7 board view and text now add all three positions for each of J1, J2, J29 and J30: pin 1 GND/switch common, center pin 2 limit signal, and the opposite pin 3 +5 V sensor supply. J-number-to-axis mapping and installed fit remain open, so no endstop route is drawn. The diagram also adds the three J3 board-view positions and two J4 switch positions; only J3's center emergency signal and J4's switch-closure-to-ground behavior are sourced, with unresolved contacts left OPEN. These are not SmoothieBox-safe wiring instructions.

The two DB25 schedules remain alternatives: J9 for the listed Mach1/Master5/TurboCNC/EMC software family, or J10 for SuperCam User 1. Their 14 STEP/DIR matches to SmoothieBox motor-control terminals remain dotted guesses because board revision, electrical compatibility and cable continuity are unverified. No limit, emergency, enable, relay or common-ground path is added.

Boxford 190VMC CNC mill — London Hackspace former loan

Wiki evidence status: exact model with machine-level dimensions, motion resolution, spindle-speed range and a controller history. The wiki marks this machine defunct and returned to its owner; these are historical machine records, not an available machine recommendation.

Identity and mechanical data

London Hackspace's wiki identifies a loaned “Boxford 190VMC,” owned by a named individual and returned to that owner. It lists eight spindle speeds from 350 to 3500 RPM, axis travel of 225 mm longitudinal × 150 mm cross × 140 mm vertical, 0.005 mm system resolution, and a 410 × 130 mm table. The page also lists 202 mm spindle-to-table distance and two 10 mm T-slots.

Control history and operation

The wiki change log records earlier operation with Boxford V5 software, followed by bCNC on Ubuntu and a later LinuxCNC configuration. A 2014 note describes a DB25 connector and says it was “almost certainly serial”; that is explicitly tentative and not a pinout. Another note mentions a 25 W serial port, but the wiki does not reconcile that statement with the controller changes. The operation section requires induction and an LDAP account, and documents use of a generic EMC2/LinuxCNC postprocessor.

Pinout and diagrams

The London Hackspace history reports a rear DB25 connector on this former-loan machine but says it was “almost certainly serial”; this is explicitly tentative and gives no signal class, mating view, contact function, voltage, or pin assignment. The 25 W wording in a separate arrival note does not resolve the interface. The current diagram therefore treats the DB25 as a machine-side peripheral and shows 25 nominal numbered positions as function-unknown OPEN inventory, not as a verified source pinout. No SmoothieBox route is established and no guess is drawn.

The same wiki records Boxford V5, bCNC on Ubuntu, and then LinuxCNC, but does not identify the fitted controller revision when the machine was returned. A separate 2014 Boxford VMC 190 conversion discussion tentatively names X/Y/Z clock and direction signals on a universal controller/stepper board, while describing wiring differences; it supplies no DB25 map and cannot be assigned to the Hackspace loan. Generic DB25/parallel-port conventions, Boxford 190VMCxi USB material, GS-D200S driver-IC pinouts, and other retrofit reports likewise do not map this connector. The linked 190VMC Programming Manual is a programming document, not evidence of this machine’s external DB25 wiring. The linked modification resources need exact source capture and variant matching before any pin roles can replace OPEN labels.

Complete wiki-researched machine dossier

Bungard CCD/MTC CNC PCB mill

Wiki evidence status: model-specific, detailed operating dossier. The Bristol Hackspace page identifies the machine as a Bungard CCD/MTC CNC modified with a replacement controller, RFID interlock, emergency stop, height mapping, and extraction. The installed controller board and its revision are not named in the captured wiki evidence.

Identity and mechanics

The wiki gives a 325 × 495 × 38 mm working envelope, a 700 × 800 × 300 mm overall size, manual tool changes, and a spindle range of 3,000–63,000 RPM. It describes two-phase stepper motors on all three axes, software-selectable 1, 1/2, and 1/4 mil step settings, and a stated precision of ±1 step. The page separately claims 20 ppm position accuracy over the work area; no measurement method or controller revision is supplied.

The bed is precision aluminium and can hold boards with double-sided tape. Spanning clamps or reference pins are noted as possible with additional accessories. A 30-degree V-bit with a 0.2 mm tip and 3.175 mm shank is recommended for isolation work; a 1.6 mm end mill is listed for outlines. The archived operator reports reasonable results with a 0.7 mm end mill.

Controller, connections, and pinout

The machine accepts G-code. The current wiki identifies Universal G-code Sender and bCNC as tested senders, a serial connection that commonly appears as COM5 or COM6, and 115200 baud. Homing is initiated with $H. It also documents an earlier Candle setup and FlatCAM workflow; those archived notes should not be assumed to describe the current controller's exact firmware or wiring.

The wiki links two controller workbooks: Control Box Connections and Control Box Connections (Alternative testing). Both direct workbook URLs returned HTTP 404 when rechecked on 2026-09-26; their contents were not recovered. No connector-to-signal pin table is transcribed here. Do not infer motor, limit, probe, spindle, or E-stop terminals from the control software or from the machine's axis count.

Operating outline from the wiki

For PCB isolation, the documented workflow is to prepare Gerber geometry in FlatCAM, export G-code, connect with bCNC or Universal G-code Sender at 115200 baud, home all axes with $H, set the XY origin by jogging, and run the toolpath. The page recommends height mapping to compensate for board non-flatness and gives sample isolation settings of 120 mm/min XY, 60 mm/min Z, 30,000 RPM, and −0.1 mm cut depth. It advises increasing PCB trace widths and clearances, with 0.5 mm and 0.4 mm respectively cited as workable minimums.

For double-sided boards the wiki describes 2 mm brass alignment pins and explicitly warns against locating an alignment hole at machine origin because the toolhead may crash on the second side. Treat these as local operating notes, not a universal setup recipe; induction is required.

Safety and visual evidence

The page requires the dust shroud and extraction system during milling, close supervision, no loose clothing or jewellery, and use of the RFID lockout. It names a Numatic Henry vacuum with HEPA filter and an emergency stop. The wiki's textual diagram caption identifies three pictured parts: the Z-axis locking bolt, the 2.5-axis skirt, and the spindle-release bolt. In 2.5D mode the spring-loaded skirt sets cut depth from tool protrusion; the locking bolt disables that movement for 3D operation. This is a mechanical orientation description, not an electrical wiring diagram.

  • PCB Mill — Bungard CCD/MTC CNC — identity, dimensions, controller workflow, process settings, archived mechanical notes, safety, and linked connection spreadsheets.
  • Electronics Room inventory — corroborates the machine's place in the current equipment list.

2026-09-26 source update · factory harness versus Bristol retrofit

The Bungard CCD factory manual (printed/PDF p. 16) identifies the signal and motor-power D-sub 15 cables as separate and non-interchangeable. It does not identify a DB25 or give contact functions. The Bristol Hackspace dossier describes a replacement controller, E-stop button, RFID lockout, height mapping and dust extraction. Its two linked Control Box Connections ODS files both returned HTTP 404 on 2026-09-26, so no retrofit pin table was recovered. Factory spindle and USB links are separate unnumbered groups; the four Bristol functions have no source-backed contact counts. All 30 factory D-sub marks remain REFERENCE ONLY / OPEN, with no inferred SmoothieBox connection.

Complete source-scoped machine dossier

CNC Automation M3X mill

Identity

Artisans Asylum calls the machine “M3X CNC Milling Machine,” maker CNC Automation, model M3X, serial 041721. The wiki notes that the nameplate says “Accu II,” while the machine's functional name is M3X; preserve both identifiers.

The owner page, retrieved for this review on 2026-09-27, describes three-axis table motion, servos and a CNC Automation control system driven by a DOS computer in the rear power box. This is source-reported architecture, not a confirmed controller-board model, fitted revision or STEP/DIR input contract. The owner page itself displays a 2025-01-21 last-updated date. [A1]

Wiki evidence

  • A1 — Artisans Asylum M3X page: machine identity and operating context; independently read in this review.
  • A2 — Annotated AccuPath rear panel: the supplied review brief reports separate PARALLEL / LPT1 DB25, RS-232 / COM 2 DB25, RS-232 / COM 1 DE-9, USB host and a “1.44 Mb” floppy-bay annotation. These are the primary agent's supplied photo observations, not a new pixel inspection by this reviewer.
  • A3 — Artisans Asylum milling-machine category: general milling context only; do not use its generic mechanism description as this installation's connector schedule.
  • A4 — CNC AccuPath M3X Operator Programming Guide: the supplied brief identifies the CNC AccuPath M3X Operator Programming Guide as an 84-page scanned 1994–2001 programming guide. The reported inspection was targeted OCR of pages 1–8 only, with G/M-code and RS-232 communications entries found in the contents. No claim of whole-manual review or electrical pin assignments follows from that limited inspection.

The annotated A2 image was inspected for its printed port labels and visible connector forms; it shows no machine motion-pin functions or cable schedule. The linked programming guide was not fully reviewed; retained local OCR covered pages 1–8 only.

Operation

The wiki describes G-code generated by CAD/CAM, optional simulation, then machining a vise-held metal workpiece. The spindle is raised/lowered and tooling changed manually. Startup involves checking the E-stop, energizing the power box, booting the DOS computer and loading a program from USB. The listed shutdown options include the front E-stop or saving/quitting before powering down. Training is required; automatic movement can start unexpectedly.

This paragraph records the owner's operating description, not a retrofit procedure or a safety-circuit schematic. Manual spindle raising/lowering and tool changing do not establish spindle-control connector functions. [A1]

Pinout and diagrams

The reviewed evidence establishes named computer I/O ports but no installed motion-controller connector pinout. The two DB25 housings are separate external machine-side peripherals: LPT1 is not COM2. No numbered PC I/O contact is promoted to an M3X axis, servo, limit, enable, return or E-stop assignment. [A1, A2]

The primary drawing includes five peripheral groups: LPT1, COM2, COM1, USB program loading and the front E-stop. Only the three named D-sub forms have individually numbered positions. USB and E-stop have OPEN group boundaries because their contact count, numbering and electrical contract are not established by the reviewed evidence. The reported floppy bay, DOS control system, servos and manual spindle/tool operation are contextual hardware, not additional selected wiring endpoints. [A1, A2]

The front E-stop remains a named safety-related control with unknown contacts and circuit. It is not mapped onto a spare endstop input. The source-reported servos do not establish a pulse-input interface. No return circuit, signal conversion, new adapter or inferred cable is drawn. [A1; review judgment]

Rendering and count semantics

The existing proposed Chapter 18 carrier schedule remains 24 exterior banks / 82 individually labeled terminals, plus four separate unnumbered service ports. Carrier terminal ordinals are not Core board pin numbers or mating-face positions. The primary M3X drawing has five peripheral groups, 59 enumerated positions, 25 generic PC-LPT source positions, 34 serial form-only positions, zero documented SmoothieBox conductors, zero dotted guesses and 59 unrouted numbered positions. Two additional unnumbered groups, USB and E-stop, have OPEN boundaries; they contribute no invented contact count.

The catalog's source flag on the 25 LPT rows records a fact in K1 only. The 34 serial rows use form_inventory_only, which the renderer already displays and counts separately. A one-line validator extension permits that existing fact category in reference-catalog rows. All three D-sub cards remain reference-layer peripherals outside SmoothieBox. OPEN means no selected route, not electrically disconnected, NC or unused. The renderer's reference_contacts count includes both reference functions and form-only rows and must not be presented as 59 electrically documented M3X pins.

Residual unknowns and acceptance boundary

The fitted computer/controller and servo-drive revisions, present-day rear-port inventory, connector sex and mating view, cable continuity, DTE/DCE configuration, electrical levels, port modes, signal polarity, returns, shielding, axis bindings, servo command/feedback interfaces and safety circuit remain unverified. Contact counts for USB and E-stop remain unknown. No machine test or powered validation has occurred in this review.

Before any electrical route is proposed, obtain revision-specific machine/controller/drive documentation and source-backed connector identification and continuity evidence. Before publication, the main agent must inspect the regenerated article and SVG in the real site, confirm all historical drawings remain collapsed and unchanged, and exercise the existing fullscreen, second-click zoom and drag-pan behavior. This is a research inventory, not a physical wiring plan.

Identity note

“Accu II” is a nameplate marking; the wiki explicitly uses M3X as the functional machine identity. Avoid counting the two strings as separate models.

Machine evidence and separate standard reference

A1 establishes owner-reported identity and operation. A2 port observations and A4 limited manual inspection are carried forward from the supplied review brief, not newly reverified pixels or PDF pages. K1 provides generic PC LPT names only; it is not an M3X motion pinout. Full source and review limits are retained in the dossier above.

IMES enclosed CNC mill — FabLab Region Nürnberg

Wiki evidence status: local machine page; the wiki lists its maker/year field as “imes BJ 2004”, type field as generic text, and current condition as limited use. Operation is permitted only together with a milling supervisor. This is a local machine identity; the exact commercial model is not established.

Machine and controls

The wiki describes an enclosed CNC mill with a 300 × 400 × 100 mm work area, a water-cooled 2.2 kW spindle with Lenze i510 drive, closed-loop steppers (StepperOnline 23HS30-5004D-E1000 motors and CL57T drives), and LinuxCNC with a Mesa 7i96S controller. The wiki characterizes it as powerful and sensitive and warns incorrect operation can damage the machine.

Local operating workflow

G-code is copied to the machine over SMB (smb://fabmill.local/), selected in the FILE view, and loaded with LOAD G-CODE. LinuxCNC checks syntax; the operator remains responsible for semantic correctness.

For startup, the wiki says to turn on the cabinet main switch and computer, check that the coolant pump is running, and open LinuxCNC. Insert and enable the key switch, release the emergency stop, activate LinuxCNC Power, then run REF ALL. The documented reference order is Z first, then X and Y. The tool must be measured with M6 G43. Manual jogging is used to set the work origin; the page warns that 100% jog speed is fast. Tool changes must use M6 G43 so offsets are set. G54 work coordinates are set with ZERO ALL or per-axis ZERO controls.

The wiki describes touching off X/Y with the cutter and gives a slow gauge-based Z-zero procedure. It warns that contacting the workpiece with the spindle damages it and says compressed air is needed for cooling. The spindle has an ER20 collet interface; the listed set covers 1–13 mm collets. The page gives example aluminium and ABS parameters, but its feed column unit is printed as “mm/m”; that ambiguity is retained and values are not normalized here.

To shut down, the wiki instructs users to turn off the computer's green main switch, press the emergency stop, clean the work area, and close the enclosure.

Pinout and visual evidence

The local wiki page's Setup, IO Mapping, and Mapping sections contain no usable machine assignment. The exact installed Mesa 7i96S revision and LinuxCNC channel map are unknown. Its manufacturer manual supplies complete TB1, TB2 and TB3 reference schedules, shown here without claiming fitted wiring or axis assignments.

The installed StepperOnline CL57T revision is unknown. The V4.1 manual names P1–P4 contacts; physical terminal order is not specified in this schedule and the fitted revision remains unverified. The wiki does not identify the Mesa-to-drive wiring, encoder wiring, motor assignment, or power connections.

The wiki names a Lenze i510 spindle drive but omits its full order code. The 11/2021 Lenze-authored family manual names X3 and X9 terminals; these remain symbolic family-reference labels. The catalog lists 109 reference positions, all OPEN, with zero proposed SmoothieBox routes or guesses. Confirm installed revisions, configuration, electrical levels and safety circuitry before any connection. Emergency-stop and enclosure interlocks must not be bypassed.

Sources

  • IMES-Fräse — FabLab Region Nürnberg Wiki — local identity, restricted status, specifications, control stack, operating sequence, tooling, and example parameters.
  • Fräse — FabLab Region Nürnberg Wiki — identifies the older donated DIY router as out of service and replaced by the IMES machine; its controller instructions are not applied to the IMES.
  • Mesa 7I96S manual V1.12 — reference terminal schedules for TB1–TB3; installed configuration unknown.
  • StepperOnline CL57T V4.1 manual — revision-specific named contacts P1–P4; installed revision and connector order unknown.
  • Lenze i510 operating instructions (11/2021) — manufacturer-authored family reference via third-party mirror; fitted order code unknown.

Unknowns: exact IMES model/nameplate and serial, Mesa revision and field-I/O assignment, CL57T revisions and all installed wiring, Lenze order code and settings, spindle/chiller details beyond those listed, latest condition and operator permissions, and the feed units shown in the local parameter table.

ISEL ICV 4030 EC

Research status: exact model name updated from the FabLab Karlsruhe machine page, which identifies its installed mill as ICV 4030 EC and links the ISEL 2017 manual. The local user guide and machine-control handbook identify the same machine operation; neither supplies a complete electrical connector pinout. References captured 2026-09-28.

Identity and local machine facts

The FabLab Karlsruhe machine page names its unit **ISEL ICV 4030 EC**. It lists 3000–24000 rpm, 300 × 400 × 140 mm travel, and 1–6 mm clamping diameter; the local guide links ISEL’s ICV 4030 EC manual. The operating guide says ProNC runs on the built-in PC. It records startup actions for the rear master switch, front PC Start/Power buttons, front E-stop, homing/reference, and work zero. These are operating instructions, not circuit assignments.

The local machine page reports that the COOLANT2 and PUMP outputs are connected to relays. It does not identify their terminal numbers, relay coil/contact wiring, ratings, or controlled loads. This dossier therefore shows a local-wiki relay group with positions unknown and no SmoothieBox route.

ISEL EC family-reference exterior interfaces

The ISEL June 2017 ICV 4030 EC manual, article number 970280 BD018 (original operating manual; revision list through 2018), describes rear-panel interfaces. It lists: RJ45 LAN to the iPC 25; USB 3.0 for external mouse/keyboard; Recovery USB 2.0 for iPC 25 recovery and external mouse/keyboard; a 15-position VGA monitor connector; M4 stud for supplementary protective equipotential bonding; 230 V AC supply inlet with main switch and two 10 A time-lag fuses; optional switched Schuko CEE7/3 socket (L/N/PE); and an optional additional 230 V AC supply inlet. The diagram treats the specified rear panel as EC family-reference evidence. Individual installed options and connector orientation have not been inspected.

The manual identifies connector form/count but does not provide a source-scoped assignment for the contacts inside LAN, USB, or VGA connectors. The diagram numbers known nominal positions as OPEN, without assigning their pin functions. For mains equipment, conductor functions L/N/PE are transcribed as connector-level reference labels only; no terminal ordering, polarity view, rating beyond cited manual text, cable, or safe retrofit is inferred. M4 is a bonding stud, not a pin.

Separate machine functions
Variant boundary

A separate 2004 ICV manual describes an earlier configuration with a DB9 acknowledgement button, 25-pin parallel interface, mains, and ground point. The FabLab page now explicitly says **ICV 4030 EC** and links the EC manual, so those earlier ICV contacts are excluded from this profile. Likewise, specifications and port layouts for the current iCV 4030EC product are not substituted for this 2017 manual. The local identity supports the EC-family reference inventory, but no serial/nameplate or rear-panel photograph confirms a particular delivered option set.

Wiring and safety status

The source-supported V2-to-machine route count is zero and the dotted-guess count is zero. OPEN means no compatible two-ended connection has been established. This is an evidence map, not a wiring instruction. Do not connect a motion controller to the proprietary drive/safety system or machine mains from these references; obtain the unit’s serial-specific wiring and qualified engineering review before any integration.

Kress CNC Portal Mill — CoMakingSpace

Wiki evidence status: local used machine, documented with controller, motors, dimensions, and operating workflow. “Kress CNC Portal Mill” is the wiki's identity; the actual frame builder and Kress spindle/router model are not identified.

Identity and components

The CoMakingSpace wiki says this portal mill was bought used in 2022 from a maker who used it to machine aluminium parts for other CNCs. It gives a 300 × 360 × 80 mm work area and describes an 80 kg steel/aluminium structure with a T-slot table. Motion uses three 23HS30-2804S stepper motors and three Leadshine DM556 drivers. The controller is an SMC5-5-N-N with a jog wheel; the listed supply is a Meanwell 48 V, 10 A unit. The spindle is described as an 800 W Chinese high-frequency spindle with an ER11 collet; exact make and electrical revision are unknown.

Operation

The wiki workflow calls for CAM output in the machine's documented G-code flavor, homing, clamping the workpiece, setting the tool and work origin, then testing new programs “in the air.” FreeCAD output uses a Mach3 post. The wiki says a supplied Fusion 360 machine/post configuration is modified because the stock Mach3 post can behave erratically with this controller. Programs are loaded from USB to the SMC5 panel.

The controller has no automatic homing sequence: the page says to run its “Origin Operation” → “Return To Home” action at session start. XYZ buttons and an X1/X10/X100 jog wheel are documented. The wiki defines machine zero at the front-left-top and negative Z motion into the work. It recommends dry-running new code and checking work zero and clearance before starting. The emergency stop cuts electricity to the spindle and stepper motors, according to the local page.

Wiring and visual evidence

The wiki names motor, drive, controller, and supply models but does not provide their terminal assignments or a verified wiring schematic. No STEP/DIR/enable, limit, spindle, or mains wiring is inferred. The wiki links a controller manual but this dossier does not use external manuals to fill gaps. The page discusses numbered panel controls and contains a coordinate-system illustration, but no connector diagram suitable for pinout transcription was available in the captured text.

OSE D3D CNC Circuit Mill

Identity

The OSE D3D CNC Circuit Mill uses the D3D Universal Axis platform strengthened/configured for PCB contact milling. The wiki distinguishes a 2018 build from a 2019 D3D Universal printer conversion, and mentions earlier pre-Universal-Axis concepts; this dossier covers the D3D Universal-axis machine.

Wiki evidence

  • OSE D3D CNC Circuit Mill build instructions: first-run electrical setup and axis-direction commissioning.
  • OSE GVCS Home List: genealogy, assembly/cut list, PCB-holder and spindle model files.
  • OSE circuit-mill model file page: CAD file history and machine image usage.

Operating/build information

The wiki's first-run sequence calls for 12 V and 48 V supply connections, RAMPS-board power, relay signal, USB to host, height probe wiring, relay switching test, dual X-stepper setup and direction verification. It says to run motion and calibration-code checks before milling. The wider build notes list frame drilling, belts/rods, bed, electronics mounting, spindle and PCB holder steps.

Pinout and diagram transcription

No complete RAMPS contact map appears in the cited build excerpt. It explicitly warns to test relay polarity (high-side versus low-side switching) and specifies a height probe and split X motion, but does not provide numbered pin assignments. Transcribe the exact machine/controller variant before wiring.

Visuals and limits

The wiki has a versioned CAD assembly and photos of axis conversion components. Genealogy distinguishes the 2018 build from a later printer conversion; do not combine their electrical or mechanical assumptions.

Roland iModela

Research status: FabLab Region Nürnberg identifies a Roland iModela (iM-01), on permanent loan and restricted-use. Captured 2026-09-23.

Wiki-listed specification

The lab page describes a small-format hobby mill for soft materials, including modelling wax, acrylic and Styrofoam, and explicitly excludes conductive materials such as metal and carbon. PCB milling is a possible use but is limited by the small motor; the machine is not presented as a general metal mill. Maximum XYZ work area is 86 × 55 × 26 mm, maximum collet-tip-to-table distance 55 mm, and maximum workpiece mass 200 g. The XYZ motors are stepper motors. The wiki lists feed ranges of 6–240 mm/min on XY and 6–180 mm/min on Z. Software resolution is 0.01 mm/step for RML-1 and 0.001 mm/step for NC code; the listed mechanical microstep resolution is 0.000186 mm/step. Supported command sets are RML-1 and NC code. These are wiki values, not independently measured values.

Wiki-recorded use and tools

The wiki identifies the machine as an iModela and documents PCB isolation milling. It records Eagle, pcp-gcode, and an iModela-specific Eagle pcb-gcode profile installed on the dedicated station. The article notes that the machine’s tool spindle accepts 2.34 mm tooling; because the lab’s other mill used 1/8-inch tools, a custom spindle adaptation was planned and its dimensions were copied locally on the wiki. The page does not establish whether that adapter was later made or installed.

The accessible machine page also contains software/file-format information for iModela Creator, Virtual MODELA, MODELA Player, 3D Engrave, SFEdit2 and ClickMILL. These are listed as available products/file types in the wiki, not as current vendor-supported versions.

Connections and pinout

No motor, limit-switch, controller, spindle-power, or communication pinout appears in the inspected wiki page (revision 3392). The 2.34 mm measurement describes the tool shank/spindle fit, not an electrical connector.

Visual evidence and source

The wiki has a local spindle-adapter drawing/PDF and two PCB-milling guide pages, but the media fetch returned a cache miss during inspection. Their content is therefore not transcribed here. FabLab Nürnberg iModela wiki page.

Evidence limits

The exact electrical controller, connector pinout, and adapter’s current installation state are not established by the accessible page. The wiki calls the unit iModela (iM-01); it also states the lab unit is a permanent loan from Roland. External links on the page were not used as factual sources; this dossier uses only wiki text and the wiki-hosted drawing reference, whose media could not be retrieved for transcription.

Wiki sources

FabLab Nürnberg wiki evidence is scoped to the iModela iM-01 listing; the local electrical controller remains unverified.

Machine research dossier · source update 2026-09-29

Identity

Artisans Asylum's wiki identifies the machine as made by Techno, model “DaVinci CNC Mill”; its serial is unknown. The linked Techno specifications page returned HTTP 502 during this review. The listing does not provide a DaVinci series/model number.

Variant references, not fitment claims

Techno’s older-model page describes model D1012 as a stepper DaVinci and model 1419 as a servo DaVinci. Since the Artisans Asylum entry says only “DaVinci CNC Mill,” the SVG shows both as separate alternative reference peripherals, with no contact positions and no SmoothieBox routes. Which drive variant is installed remains OPEN.

Manual scope and pinout

The linked 81-page Techno CNC Servo GCODE Interface manual (Build #377) documents software operation, including X/Y and optional A-axis controls, spindle/coolant controls, and a PC PCI-interface/control-box arrangement. It is not a DaVinci electrical schematic. Its conditional controller-card/riser setup does not establish hardware fitted to this unit. No machine-specific connector positions, pin assignments, or DB25 schedule were found. The machine-side contact inventory is therefore empty: 0 numbered contacts, 0 routes, and 0 guesses. Every proposed SmoothieBox contact remains unconnected; “OPEN” is an unresolved path, not an electrical NC designation.

Operating information and unknowns

The local wiki page has safety, materials, operation, and maintenance headings without substantive procedures in the retrieved text. The installed DaVinci variant, serial, drive/controller revision, all machine-side connectors and pin assignments, wiring ratings/polarity, and harness state remain unknown. Do not use this diagram to wire the machine.

The HSBNE machine wiki links the HILDI project. Its LinuxCNC 2.8 configuration, generated 2021-10-20, selects a Mesa 7i76E. The official Mesa manual supplies numbered TB2–TB6 board contact functions; the dated HILDI HAL file maps X/Y/Z step generation, selected home/probe/MPG inputs, spindle enable, coolant flood and status lights.

This source does not establish that the 2021 configuration or board revision is currently installed, the machine harness landing points, external signal levels/polarity, or a compatible SmoothieBox route.     2026-09-26 manual-image reinspection

    The owner’s two-page YUHAI manual image supplies 31 distinct printed numeric positions and an FG shell mark. Its CN3 section and CN1 running header conflict; +24VIN and /CLR both use printed 24, while /PAO and alternate T-REF overlap at 11. The LinuxCNC build thread reports Chinese servo drives and step/direction control, but neither the image nor thread verifies the installed drive brand/model/revision, chosen connector variant or cabinet pin-to-pin route. These are source-manual reference marks only. Zero SmoothieBox routes or dotted guesses are selected.

    schuetzbuilds' MAHO MH600T LinuxCNC retrofit

    Partial interface evidence

    LinuxCNC Forum member schuetzbuilds and his brother identify their machine as a MAHO MH600T originally fitted with a Heidenhain 332 control. The compact control module also contained EXE interfaces; the owners replaced those with three EXE602 modules to read the machine's linear scales. The thread says the C axis was initially ignored.

    Forum-reported build status: X/Y/Z motion and some relay functions worked, but the hydraulic pump tripped the stop chain and full commissioning remained open.

    What is still missing

    Configuration-specific insert. Confirm actual hardware, contact orientation, electrical levels, wire identity, and safety function before a V2-Core label. Do not apply the 67126 color map to an unidentified motor. Driver-board H3 removes power immediately but is not a certified E-stop.

    Sherline 8760 DB25 high is >2 V and low <0.5 V; the active-low step pulse is at least 22 μs. The driver-box supply is 24 V DC / 4 A and is not the DB25 logic rating. DIN motor wiring is a separate winding-output domain. 8760 product specification.

    Documented evidence · unresolved wiring

    Documented: 8760 product wiring and P/N67126 motor spec, 2020-03-10 pp. 1–2. 8760 DB25 2/3 X, 4/5 Y, 6/7 Z, 8/9 A are box logic inputs even if lathe uses fewer axes; 5-pin DIN motor lead colors only for specified motor as #008. Unresolved: installed lathe axis wiring and unused-axis behavior; do not relabel a mill Y pin as lathe Z without actual configuration.

    Complete wiki-researched machine dossier

    Millport SmartLathez 1740 CNC lathe

    Identity

    Artisans Asylum identifies a Millport SmartLathez 1740, serial 622005, with a Centroid controller. The site also operates a separate Tormach 15L Slant-Pro family; this dossier covers the Millport only.

    Wiki evidence

    • Artisans Asylum machine page: maker/model/serial, safety/training, CAM workflow and machine use.
    • Artisans Asylum CNC lathe workflow: startup, tool offsets, workholding and turning-operation notes specific to the SmartLathez 1740.
    • Artisans Asylum metal lathe safety/category: shared hazard guidance.

    Operating information

    The wiki describes loading G-code from a USB drive, checking way oil/coolant, powering and homing the machine, loading the program and reviewing its toolpath before setting tool offsets. It names Centroid control and Tri-Cool coolant. The wiki warns that the tailstock can trip the furthest Z limit and that a default parting feed can destroy tooling; use current training and verified setup values.

    Visuals and pinout

    The wiki has machine/safety images and a linked manual. No numbered controller or connector pinout was established from the wiki pages reviewed.

    Source inconsistencies

    The wiki's manual link and operating notes should be checked against the installed controller revision. No electrical assignments are reproduced here.

    Wiki sources

    Sources are restricted to the supplied wiki-research dossier. External vendor/forum links are not used as evidence.

    Documented evidence · unresolved wiring

    Documented / version scope: Revision conflict requiring explicit source labeling, not a simple mislabel: The Avid 2020Q3.1 PDF has 20.1 in its filename but its cover and every page header say “17.4 Electronics Revision” (PDF pp. 1, 17–18). Its CRP850 table on PDF p. 18 has 42 terminals: 33/34 spindle relay FWD/DCM, 35/36 PWM/5V ground, 37/38 0–10V/analog common, 39/40 12V input/ground, 41/42 fault/ground. Conversely Avid's current 17.4 HTML schematic, CRP850 Phoenix terminal table, has 36 terminals: 27/28 FWD/DCM, 29/30 PWM/5V ground, 31/32 0–10V/12V ground, 33/34 12V input/ground, 35/36 fault/ground. Both Avid documents claim the same 17.4 electronics revision and CRP850-00E, yet their numbering and extra terminals materially disagree. Avid manual revision index places 17.4 purchases in Sep2017–Dec2019 and 20.1 in Jan2020–Mar2021; this makes the filename suspicious but does not override the PDF's explicit 17.4 headers. The official 20.1 HTML schematic independently shows the same 42-terminal table, including 33/34 FWD/DCM and 37/38 analog, as the disputed PDF. This strongly suggests stale 17.4 page headers in the PDF, but that remains an inference; the filename plus table agreement do not justify silently overriding its printed revision. The cited PDF must be read alongside the conflicting 17.4 HTML and matching 20.1 HTML, then require physical board/photo/part revision or manufacturer clarification before any 17.4 terminal label. Both documents' peripheral 14-pin table uses 7 FWD, 8 DCM, 9 analog, 10 analog common; the PDF prose says 8/9 for analog despite table and board text saying 9/10. 17.4 HTML also publishes DB9 NEMA23 motor outputs (1/5 current-set resistor, 2–4 NC, 6 B+ yellow, 7 B− blue, 8 A+ red, 9 A− green) and XLR NEMA34 motor outputs (1 A+ red, 2 A− green, 3 B+ yellow, 4 B− blue). Motor contacts are phase outputs, not step/dir. Unresolved: identify installed CRP850 physical layout and exact dated manual; source discrepancy is unresolved, not corrected by choosing either map.

    Documented evidence · unresolved wiring

    Documented: Onefinity official packing forum post, axis-to-controller motor output map M0 X, M1 Y, M2 Y, M3 Z; Buildbotics manual v1.0, 25-pin I/O and motor port sections, old 12–36 V hardware. M ports are motor phase outputs, not step/dir; manual gives four-contact motor layout upper-left B+, lower-left B−, lower-right A+, upper-right A−. Old manual DB25 pin 6 and pin 20 are +3.3 V, pin 17 PWM, pin 15 enable, pin 16 direction, 22 probe, 23 E-stop. New Buildbotics manual v2.0 gives pin 6 0–10 V on 24–48 V controller; never transfer to Gen1 without board identification. Buildbotics I/O breakout warns M and M2 variants have different pinouts. Unresolved: Onefinity firmware/hardware revision, motor connector face and E-stop safety; v1.0 E-stop is software controlled, not certified.

    Source-reviewed machine interface dossier

    Blue Elephant ELE1325ATC-R · Bumblebee

    Evidence scope: HSBNE identifies this sheet router as Blue Elephant ELE1325ATC-R, called Bumblebee, and links Syntec 6 documentation; the fitted controller model and revision are not identified. The local operational guide describes workflow and controls, not electrical terminals. Generic Syntec documents remain reference-only and are not transferred to this machine.

    Machine identity and operating context

    The HSBNE page describes an approximately 1300 × 2500 mm bed, ISO30 tooling and an eight-position automatic tool changer. It gives conflicting spindle entries (18,000 rpm versus 9 kW / 24,000 rpm), which remain unresolved. Its “X/Y/Z + A/Y2” notation and a rotary-looking fixture do not establish a fitted fourth-axis configuration.

    The operational guide names X−, Y−, Z+ and 4+ homing indicators; E-stop controls on the controller and both gantry sides; ATM tool-length measurement; USB file import; and a 0.73 MPa pressure alarm. These identify functions and operator controls, not switch or controller terminals, connector counts, polarity, or safety-circuit topology. Its fourth-axis workflow does not identify installed axis wiring.

    Controller references and limits

    The linked Syntec 6 Series Operation Manual is a generic manual dated 2014-03-02, version 1.21. It does not establish the HSBNE machine's controller model/revision or cabinet terminal schedule. Blue Elephant's generic buyer guide describes Syntec 6MB capacity as 32 inputs and 32 outputs and gives an example four-axis ATC allocation of 8 outputs and 13 inputs. Those are logical-capacity/example figures, not physical contact counts or fitted assignments. The guide says its standard circuit drawing is available only through a separate technical-exchange group; that drawing is not present here.

    The separate Mach3 USB manual covers another control architecture and is excluded from the P1P/Syntec assessment. No exact-machine source establishes a DB25, so this profile shows none. No source supports a machine pin map, route, or guess.

    Machine and reference panel inventory

    The current diagram has seven panels: three named machine groups—controller logic/communication; motors, spindle and ATC; and homing, tool-length measurement, E-stop and protective/pressure functions—plus four reference-only source panels. The four reference panels have zero contacts. Across the diagram there are zero numbered machine contacts, zero numbered reference contacts, zero candidate routes and zero guesses. The 82 SmoothieBox exterior positions are shown as its own proposed case inventory and do not prove a machine connection.

    Sources

    • HSBNE Blue Elephant / Bumblebee machine page — identity, machine description and linked controller-family documentation.
    • HSBNE operational guide — operating sequence, homing indicators, E-stop locations, ATM, USB file import and pressure alarm; no electrical terminal schedule.
    • Syntec 6 Series Operation Manual, v1.21 (2014-03-02) — generic controller operation reference only.
    • Blue Elephant generic CNC-router buyer guide — Syntec 6MB logical-capacity and example ATC allocation; not a fitted terminal map.
    • Original HSBNE machine photograph · retained local image — model name and visible machine form only.
    • Mach3 USB controller manual — excluded — different control architecture; not used to infer this Syntec machine's connectors or DB25.

    Profile sources

    HSBNE's model-specific records support identity and operator workflow. Syntec/Blue Elephant references are generic and do not establish fitted hardware or terminal assignments.

    EleksMill CNC router — CoMakingSpace

    Wiki evidence status: named small CNC router documented as a working learning machine. The exact EleksMill generation and controller hardware are not specified.

    Machine details

    The CoMakingSpace wiki describes an EleksMill brought into the space as a small machine for learning CNC routing. The page lists a 130 × 90 × 40 mm working range, notes that available Z clearance depends on endmill length, and says the machine has no endstops. Foam is the only material currently listed for use; 1/8-inch end mills are named.

    Workflow

    The wiki says to create a toolpath in CAD/CAM software such as Fusion 360, choose a GRBL postprocessor, secure the material, home/jog and set work coordinates, then send G-code. It compares the workflow to the larger WorkBee router. The source page notes that it is a CNC-router introduction machine; it does not provide a tested speed/feed table.

    Pinouts and visual evidence

    No controller make/model, axis wiring, motor pinout, limit-switch map, or electrical diagram is provided. The note that it has no endstops is a machine-level limitation, not a connector map. The wiki page includes a photograph captioned as routing styrofoam; it does not expose a wiring or dimensioned mechanical drawing in the captured page text.

    Sources

    • EleksMill — machine identity, range, material, tool size, and no-endstop note.
    • CNC Router — machine is listed among the space's CNC routers.

    Unknowns: variant/revision, control electronics, exact axis travel measurement convention, homing method, safe feed/speed settings, and all connector pinouts.

    Complete wiki-researched machine dossier

    Maslow4 large-format CNC router

    Wiki evidence status: Appropedia has a catalogue entry and a dedicated machine article. This dossier uses both Appropedia wiki pages only. It describes the Maslow4 design, not a verified local installation or a particular controller-board revision.

    Machine and motion system

    The dedicated Appropedia article calls Maslow4 a compact, portable, large-format CNC router and the 2023 generation of the Maslow CNC family. It states a working format up to 8 × 4 ft and says the machine can operate from horizontal to nearly vertical (up to 75°). Four steel-reinforced belts constrain the router's position against four rigid anchor points; those points need not form a precisely spaced rectangle.

    The router is carried by a sled. Four articulated arms pay belt in or out to position the sled; two Z-axis stepper motors move the router vertically. The article describes belt-length measurement using magnetic encoders and automatic calibration from measurements taken while the belts are tensioned.

    Controls and operation

    The wiki says the machine creates its own Wi-Fi network or can join a local network, then exposes a browser-based control interface. It also identifies Bluetooth and USB-C connections. The WebUI loads standard G-code, reports machine status, runs calibration, and displays job progress. The wiki describes the firmware as a Maslow-specific branch of FluidNC (formerly Grbl_Esp32).

    The article describes automatic calibration, browser control, and G-code operation, but does not give a safe step-by-step commissioning or cutting procedure. This dossier therefore does not turn the design description into a complete operating instruction.

    Electronics and interfaces

    The wiki describes a custom five-axis control board with an ESP32-S3, four DC servo motors and magnetic encoders, two Z-axis stepper motors, onboard SD storage, and a cooling fan. It says motor-driver boards sit between the controller and the DC servos. These functional descriptions do not identify connector pins or establish cable-level assignments.

    Visuals and pinouts

    The Appropedia article presents machine, arm, and controller-board images with explanatory captions. The visible captions identify the four arms, router, sled, Z steppers, belt spool, geared DC motor, encoder PCB, and belt end. No readable electrical schematic or connector contact map is supplied in the inspected article; no pins are inferred.

    Sources

    • Tolocar/Maslow4 — Appropedia wiki — design overview, kinematics, electronics, firmware, and assembly.
    • Tolocar/Open Source Machine Tools — Appropedia wiki — catalogue cross-reference and 8 × 4 ft description.

    Unknowns: exact controller PCB revision, contact-level wiring, servo-driver part numbers, specific router installation, machine calibration results, and cutting parameters for a given material/tool.

    2026-09-26 original-PCB source update

    The MaslowCNC five-motor control-board schematic, commit 04e8d4e3e2f5a23d3ec3cd393bd7e60005cba998, supports 48 physical positions across belt-motor, Z-stepper, encoder, Aux, Serial, fan and XT60 power interfaces. The separate encoder-board schematic adds five U2 positions; its fifth is unconnected, while the main board’s fifth encoder-header contacts are GND. Those 53 design marks are OPEN references, not evidence of installed PCB revision, cable orientation or channel-to-arm matching. The carried router is a separate mains-powered appliance in the design overview; these schematics establish no contact-level router power or control connection. The XT60 source symbol does not establish a fitted supply rating or cable. No SmoothieBox conductor or function guess is selected.

    Munich Maker Lab custom CNC router

    Research capture: 2026-09-23; source rechecked 2026-09-26. Status: historical-build dossier integrated as one atlas profile. Current installed wiring remains unverified.

    Identity, revision and deduplication

    Named custom machine in Munich Maker Lab’s archived CNC router build, with v1.1 material dated 2021-04-09 and later page edits. This is not the Genmitsu machine currently listed elsewhere at the lab. Its CSMIO/IP-M/Mach3 arrangement does not make it the atlas’s generic Mach3 parallel-port profile. A shared control program is not a shared machine identity. Count the named physical build once; controller changes are revisions, not additional machines.

    Archived build page (observed oldid 9625). Community records combine historical wiring and later modifications; current physical conformity is unknown.

    Machine and control facts

    The wiki describes Mach3 with replacement CSMIO/IP-M, three 70 V / 400 W motor supplies, a 24 V-release Z brake, and water-cooled ER20 spindle rated 2.2 kW, 8000–24000 rpm with HY02D223B drive. Setup, driver and safety-circuit details must remain installation-specific. This record does not establish a complete safe operating procedure. Build source.

    Probotix Fireball V90 CNC router

    Research status: wiki-sourced machine-specific dossier; the MakeICT wiki marks the machine retired. Captured 2026-09-23.

    Identity and status

    MakeICT’s equipment inventory identifies a Probotix Fireball V90 CNC mill/router and marks it retired. The associated V90 wiki page preserves a user guide. It is not evidence of a currently usable machine.

    Wiki-recorded configuration and use

    • Bed: 12 × 18 inches; cutting area: 11 × 17 inches.
    • Z travel: 3 inches minus cutter length.
    • Input: G-code. The wiki names pycam for STL-to-G-code and describes other software that had been used.
    • 1/8-inch shanks are listed. The article warns that small bits break easily and describes the cone/collet orientation.
    • Limit switches are in series: the guide says a trip stops the machine but does not identify which switch caused it.
    • An E-stop to the right of the screen stops movement but does not turn off the router.
    • The G-code cutting-motor control is reported inactive; the router motor is switched and speed-adjusted with hardware controls.

    Wiki-transcribed control facts

    The page lists G20/G21 unit selection, G00 rapid positioning, G01 feed movement, and G90/G91 absolute/relative positioning. It warns to raise Z before rapid moves and to ask for experienced help before attempting aluminium. Steel is explicitly discouraged because the frame is not suitable.

    Connections and pinout

    CircuitWiki evidencePinout
    Limit switchesSeries-connected according to the wikiNo connector or conductor assignments given
    E-stopStops motion, leaves router poweredNo contact/polarity/safety-chain diagram
    Router power/speedControlled with hardware switch and internal speed-control knobNo terminal map or voltage details
    Stepper driversWiki warns to disable motors before moving a tripped axis and says an earlier driver failedNo board/driver pinout

    Optional Probotix motor/driver kit and DB25 reference

    The Probotix legacy V90 guide says its basic motor/driver kit includes motors, drivers, a breakout board, power supply, a DB25 cable, and an IDC cable connecting the drivers to the breakout board. The same guide says a complete running machine needs a PC with a parallel port, while its base V90 kit is mechanical only and includes no motors or electronics. This is optional kit context, not evidence that the retired MakeICT V90 has those electronics. The guide gives no DB25 pin functions, connector-end direction, mating-face view, or breakout-board revision. The SmoothieBox diagram therefore treats the DB25 as a machine-side peripheral reference, lists its 25 nominal pin positions individually, and leaves every position OPEN.

    Shapeoko 2 source reconciliation · 2026-09-28

    This profile is based on the pinned RaumZeitLabor Shapeoko 2 revision 16813 and linked TinyG settings revision 16658. Both describe historical shop state; current hardware fitment is unverified.

    Machine equipment and control

    The page identifies a 300 W Quiet Cut spindle and says TinyG can command spindle speed and on/off through G-code. No spindle contact schedule, control levels, power wiring or SmoothieBox endpoint is given, so spindle wiring remains OPEN. The equipment list names a machine emergency-stop button, while its planning list also says to add an emergency-stop button at the machine. The source does not resolve installed status or describe contacts, a safety loop or an interlock; no E-stop route is proposed.

    The equipment list counts eight microswitches for homing/endstops. Their individual positions are not enumerated. The sensor socket below has six signal positions, while the saved configuration enables A-min homing without naming a physical connector. The eight switches cannot be mapped from this evidence.

    TinyG saved configuration · 2016-11-08

    The linked dump identifies TinyG ID 3X3566-JL2, firmware build 440.20, version 0.97, hardware version 8, normally-closed switch type, USB baud 115200 and flow control off. The machine page separately states that the serial default is 115200 8N1 with hardware flow control; the saved configuration differs from that generic default note. The archived configuration is scoped only to the named 2016 snapshot.

    Saved axis modes: X-min and Y-min are limit plus homing; X-max and Y-max are limit-only; Z-min is off; Z-max is homing-only; A-min is homing-only; A-max is off. This software configuration does not assign physical connector positions. Because the sensor map labels contact 7 “Z min / probe” but the saved config disables Z-min, that dual-purpose contact remains OPEN. A-min has no matching physical socket signal in this table and also remains OPEN.

    Drag-chain motor cable conductor labels

    Printed conductor ordinals are cable-core numbers, not motor-connector cavity positions. The general order is 1 red B1/B+, 2 blue B2/B−, 3 green A1/A−, 4 black A2/A+. The separate X-stepper exception is 1 green A1, 2 red B1, 3 black A2, 4 blue B2. The source says green and black are swapped on the left Y stepper, but does not tabulate its resulting core/contact map. None of these motor references maps to a SmoothieBox driver input.

    Identity and deployment

    Quelab names the machine Shop Sabre Sidekick 12. Its wiki says it was donated by Ideum Inc. in 2021, weighed over 3000 lb, and was moved and installed by a professional rigging crew. A member added warning lights and additional E-stops and brought the machine to a usable state. The wiki calls it a red-level tool and requires training/certification.

    Wiki-recorded use

    The page says Vectric VCarvePro Makerspace Edition is used to prepare files, which can be created on a personal computer and brought to the machine. It does not document a complete local setup, postprocessor, tool-change, homing, or machining procedure.

    Connections and pinout

    The wiki confirms additional emergency-stop buttons and warning lights were installed, but provides no circuit diagram, contact numbers, voltage, interlock, spindle, axis-drive, or pendant wiring. The E-stop count and physical locations need current on-site verification.

    StepCraft 2/600

    Research status: wiki-sourced CNC build/maintenance dossier; distinct model size from the already-documented StepCraft 840. Captured 2026-09-23.

    Identity and wiki history

    FabLab Karlsruhe’s project wiki calls the machine “Step-Craft 600 CNC-Fräse” and identifies the product variant as “Step-Craft 2/600.” The wiki records a 432 × 680 mm clamping area, 420 × 600 × 140 mm working envelope, and 175 mm clearance height. Its HF spindle is listed at 500 W maximum with 0.1–6 mm collets; the page lists 220 V supply.

    Use and maintenance evidence

    The page records WinPC NC and Autodesk Fusion 360 in the software section. The historical build log reports alignment work, Y-axis step-loss problems, rebuilding/adjusting the axis system, and an eventual successful 2 mm aluminium trial, followed later by another failed trial with step loss and removal for investigation. The wiki explicitly says there is no regular operating log and that the machine was handed to experienced users. Treat it as an archived/project machine, not as confirmed operational today.

    Connections and pinout

    The wiki mentions USB full version and a powered HF spindle but supplies no wiring schematic, connector names, pin numbers, voltage signals, or axis-drive assignments. A table/outlet E-stop is mentioned as part of the build, without electrical details.

    Visual evidence and source

    The wiki page includes a machine image and maintenance/build records. No electrical diagram was present in the inspected text. FabLab Karlsruhe Step-Craft 600 project wiki.

    Evidence limits

    All performance/history claims are attributed to the project wiki and date-specific entries. The wiki links to non-wiki product pages; those are not used as evidence here. Exact drive/controller revision and current location/status are not established.

    2026-09-28 staged manufacturer schedule before route review, retained

    Manufacturer reference only — not the FabLab Winti machine pinout. The STEPCRAFT SC2 v5.1 manual covers the 840 size and gives unit-control/optional-module schedules for X1, X2 and optional 4th-axis X101. The Winti page does not identify the installed generation, controller or fitted options. The tables preserve each manual position as a machine-side reference peripheral; they do not establish fitment, connector orientation, shell/gender, electrical compatibility or a cable. X1 is named only as a 25-position LPT adapter; DB-25 shell/gender is unverified. Every contact remains OPEN pending route review. STEPCRAFT SC2 v5.1 manual, §6.5; FabLab Winti source page.

    Research capture: 2026-09-23. Status: wiki-grounded draft; integration and whole-repository deduplication pending.

    Identity, use and deduplication

    FabLab Winti’s Stepcraft 840. Generation, drive/controller revision and spindle model are unknown. Checked against Shapeoko, OpenBuilds, Avid, Genmitsu and other atlas routers; Stepcraft 840 is separately named, not an alias or controller change.

    Wiki-supported machine facts

    Community page documents a gantry mill/router. Its cutting examples are explicitly anecdotal and depend on tooling/material condition, so this dossier does not promote them to machine limits or universal feeds. Community machine page.

    Control, setup and use

    The annotated bed image can support fixture planning only after checking units and the actual installation. The wiki’s material-specific examples are starting evidence for a later setup guide; controller initialization, postprocessor and safe homing sequence remain unknown in inspected sources. Community machine page.

    Connections and pinout

    Circuit / connectorPin/contact and signalDirection / polarityElectrical detailsEvidence status
    Controller logic and communicationUnknown physical connector pin assignmentsUnknownUnknownNo machine-specific contact map found in inspected wiki sources
    Motors and spindleUnknown contact assignmentsUnknownOnly the separately cited component ratings are knownDo not translate a motor rating into logic voltage
    Limits, probe, E-stop and protective circuitsUnknownUnknownUnknownButton appearance and workflow do not identify safety wiring

    Visual evidence and transcription

    Wiki source page · Original wiki-hosted media · Retained original.

    Image transcription: green dashed rectangle “600 × 840”; green diagonal “140”; blue overall arrows “612” across and “920” along; hole pitch arrows “80” in both directions and “M6”; coordinate arrows x right, y up, z out of page. Red mushrooms appear at opposite corners. Units and the meaning of diagonal 140 are not written in the image: do not silently call it Z travel.

    The image belongs to its source; retaining it records research evidence and does not assert ownership or a reuse license. Consult the source for licensing before republication.

    Conflicts and open questions

    Visual dimensions are labels, not an independently checked travel specification. Connector and stop-contact assignments are absent.

    Evidence limits and integration gate

    This is a wiki-derived dossier, not a manufacturer-certified wiring instruction. Unknown means the inspected sources did not establish that field. A photographed stop button does not establish its contact logic, safety rating, or interlock circuit. Do not infer a machine pinout from its software, controller family, cable color, or connector appearance.

    Deduplication was checked against the complete frozen atlas-label inventory supplied in the native fallback payload, including the prior controller leads. The rest of the repository and concurrent new dossiers were not inspected by this advisor. The parent must perform that broader check before crediting this toward 100 new machines.

    Sources and applicability

    The community page identifies the Winti machine. Manufacturer sources describe separate family/optional-module schedules; their fitment and electrical compatibility remain unresolved.

    Codex session transcript: /home/arthur/.codex/sessions/2026/09/29/rollout-2026-09-29T00-17-19-01a0ea18-0cc6-7572-80b5-d148b73b69ab.jsonl

    RichAuto’s official A18 product page identifies a four-axis system with an 8-input/8-output interface board and a 50-core cable; its parameter table separately says “Controlled Axis Number 3 axis.” The common A1X manual has generic interface-board output/input schedules, while its A18-specific §8.2 table provides the A18 input functions. Those are controller-side reference marks only: the SoMakeIt page does not identify the installed terminal board, 50-core conductor mapping, drivers, or cabinet handoff.

    The full listed schedules are kept separate below. X01–X08 differ between generic A1X §3.2 and A18-specific §8.2: generic X04 is tool setting and X08 pedal switch; A18 §8.2 assigns X04 A-axis zero and X08 E-stop. The A18 output schedule is not reconstructed from generic terminal references. The generic A1X fourth-axis output group is labelled C_AXIS while the A18 input chapter uses A; the wiring manual and product page do not map the particular machine harness between those marks.

    Every listed position is OPEN to SmoothieBox. The A18 pulse/direction marks are controller outputs; the driver inputs and any safe controller changeover are undocumented. No dotted route is justified. The SoMakeIt rotary group has no numbered contacts, mist coolant remains pneumatic, and no DB25 is established.

    Diagram update: the selected SmoothieBox figure now contains eight separate RichAuto reference cards with all 48 manufacturer-listed marks, all OPEN, alongside the 82-contact proposed SmoothieBox exterior. It shows zero guessed paths and keeps the rotary and mist-coolant groups as unknown-contact machine-side peripherals. The previous selected SVG is preserved byte-for-byte in the archive (SHA-256 cdf40107626f75e9ea3ca0f0c18f50735b59736435f1e7c3e0be0df4dc1970f4).

    Complete wiki-researched machine dossier

    StyleCNC STM6090

    Research status: wiki-sourced machine dossier; exact model absent from the frozen atlas and exact-name repository search. Captured 2026-09-23.

    Identity and configuration

    SoMakeIt identifies a four-axis (XYZ plus rotary) StyleCNC STM6090 with a 600 × 900 mm bed, 600 × 750 × 150 mm effective work volume, and RichAuto A18 controller. The space notes modifications for coolant and dust collection. Its controller is operated from the machine; the wiki reports Vectric VCarve Makerspace Edition on a nearby PC for CAM.

    Wiki-recorded workflow

    1. Create a CAD model and generate G-code with CAM.
    2. The wiki says the default controller workflow has the spindle on and feeds/speeds selected through a menu before running a program; its intermediate page covers configuring these from G-code.
    3. The wiki describes a mist-coolant setup for aluminium and similar materials. For wood, it instructs users to raise the mist head and disconnect the air supply. Its page states a 5% coolant-oil / 95% distilled-water mix.
    4. Four-axis use is not fully described: the wiki says VCarve substitutes rotary moves for X or Y and therefore does not provide true simultaneous four-axis paths; manual moves or software with the needed feature are required.

    Connections and pinout

    Complete wiki-researched machine dossier

    Ooznest WorkBee CNC router — CoMakingSpace configuration

    Wiki evidence status: exact WorkBee-family installation with substantial local mechanical and controls information. The wiki identifies this installation as a 1500 × 1500 mm WorkBee based on the OpenBuilds OX; it does not identify a specific WorkBee hardware revision.

    Machine and installed components

    The wiki reports a roughly 1280 × 1200 mm cutting area and material up to 50 mm thick. Its surfaced spoilboard area is 1260 × 1160 mm, within a 1445 × 1370 mm total spoilboard. In the first half of 2024 it received an electrical overhaul: Duet 3 6HC+ controller, RepRapFirmware, web and touch interfaces, MT-2303HS280AW 2.8 A NEMA23 stepper motors, and a DeWalt D26200 router. The wiki calls the machine based on the OpenBuilds OX; this documents the local assembly, not a claim that all WorkBee kits use these electronics.

    Motion and calibration notes

    The CoMakingSpace change log says X travel was about 1.1% off and records a later M92 configuration change from X3.361 Y3.331 Z400 to X3.324 Y3.331 Z400. Treat these as a dated local configuration note, not portable settings. The page says the FreeCAD RRF post-processor needs special settings; Fusion 360 also has machine-specific settings.

    Operation

    The wiki describes a CNC-router introduction prerequisite, CAM toolpath generation, workpiece clamping, appropriate collet and bit selection, homing, setting the workpiece origin, uploading G-code, personal protection, and keeping an emergency stop available. The DeWalt D26200 router is reported to run at 16,000–27,000 RPM, with 8 mm, 6 mm, 1/4-inch, and 1/8-inch collets listed. Extraction starts with the spindle; a cyclone separator is fitted before the shop vacuum.

    Pinouts and diagrams

    The wiki names the Duet 3 6HC+ mainboard and stepper type but supplies no connector-to-axis assignment, motor coil pinout, limit-switch map, spindle control wiring, or complete electrical schematic. The dated change log mentions defective crimps on the Duet board and their replacement. Do not infer connector contacts from the controller model alone. The retrieved wiki pages provided textual specifications and operation notes, but no connection diagram suitable for pinout transcription.

    Sources

    • WorkBee — installation size, work area, router, motors/controller, calibration log and extraction.
    • CNC Router — local installation overview, router RPM/collets, spoilboard and postprocessor notes.
    • CNC Mills and Routers — current machine-category index.

    Unknowns: kit/hardware revision, complete wiring and pin assignments, controller firmware build, and the currently loaded exact machine-configuration file.

    Interface reading

    What is still missing

    Need exact PSU manufacturer sheet. Confirm actual hardware, contact orientation, electrical levels, wire identity, and safety function before a V2-Core label. Match the actual PSU label and terminal order before using that supplier manual; do not promote this row to a universal K40 map.

    The secondary K40 example names PSU L−, FG, AC, G, P/WP, L/TL, IN, 5V and +24V; PSU variants and permit/fire circuits differ. A 3.3 V controller may require a compatible 5 V interface. SmoothK40 blue-box guide; Second blue-box PSU guide.

    Documented evidence · unresolved wiring

    Documented: MYJG-40W V20220713 manual is one PSU variant, not a generic K40. Secondary K40.se PSU survey documents multiple MYJG variants and connector differences; LightObject PSU article likewise shows differing port-B arrangements.     Current source-scoped external-interface evidence

    The current Attraktor page identifies a BRM 90130 and documents a 150 W tube plus matching PSU replacement in 2024. The separate BRM Version 2 manual is dated 2016-04-09 and printed pp. 26–29 document its model-level chiller hoses/alarm cable, compressor, exhaust/BOFA, PC/USB/mouse/network interfaces and control-panel emergency stop. Printed p. 120 is a power/electrical schematic, not an external low-voltage pinout. The manual and current Attraktor page do not provide a fitted controller revision, numbered external contact map, machine harness schedule, or laser-PSU control terminals. All such machine contacts and SmoothieBox routes remain OPEN.

    The chiller alarm is a documented cutting-safety dependency. The rear 230/240 V, 50 Hz extractor socket is mains context only. Neither is represented as a SmoothieBox GPIO route. No dotted function guess is justified by the available pin-level evidence.

    Complete wiki-researched machine dossier

    Just Add Sharks Silvertail A0 laser cutter

    Wiki evidence status: exact machine model independently named by London Hackspace and Bristol Hackspace. London records a 130 W tube and 1200 × 900 mm cutting area. The two wiki pages establish the same model family, but do not prove that the two sites have identical hardware revisions.

    Identity and operation

    London Hackspace identifies its machine as “Just Add Sharks Silvertail A0,” purchased by pledge in 2014. Its wiki lists a 1200 × 900 mm cutting area and a 130 W laser tube. It requires induction and membership, and it stresses continuous supervision because of fire risk. Its instructions require the CO2 extinguisher, water pump and extractor to be ready, and coolant at 22 ± 3 °C. The operating page describes LightBurn, places the software origin at the bed's top-left corner, and explains focusing relative to a ruler on the cutting bed.

    Bristol Hackspace's current equipment catalogue separately lists an “A0 Laser Cutter - Just Add Sharks Silvertail,” corroborating the model name at a second wiki site. That listing does not expose a Bristol-specific power or work-area value.

    Pinout and diagram evidence

    The London Hackspace LightBurn repository supplies an MKS V1.0 Smoothieboard-clone config snapshot. It lists X STEP 2.2!, DIR 2.3!, ENABLE 0.4; Y STEP 0.19!, DIR 0.20!, ENABLE 0.10; Z STEP 2.13!, DIR 0.11!, ENABLE 0.19; X-min 1.29!^, X-max 1.28!^, Y-min 1.27!^, Y-max 1.26!^; Z-max 1.24!^ is defined despite gamma_limit_enable false and home_to_min, while Z-min 1.25^ is commented out; laser PWM is 2.0 (20 µs) and M3/M5 fire output is 1.23. These are logical configuration entries, not physical connector positions or proof of fitted switches. The config gives no physical switch-terminal layouts or separate endstop GND/return contacts, so those remain unknown rather than inferred. The source assigns Y STEP and Z ENABLE to the same MCU pin P0.19; this unresolved conflict is not silently corrected. The MYJG-80R manual reference names H, L, P, G, IN and 5V control terminals. The two dotted guesses are PWM.1 to IN through an unspecified conversion interface and PWM.3 GND to G as a possible signal reference. H and L stay OPEN: firmware semantics and terminal polarity do not reveal the installed carrier conversion or endpoint. DOTTED = GUESS. The historical MKS +5 V level-shift note does not qualify SmoothieBox voltage, polarity, isolation or wiring. No route is wiring guidance.

    Supplemental controller and operating-state history

    London Hackspace upgrade notes distinguish the stock LaserCut 5.3 setup from a later Smoothieware/LightBurn arrangement. They describe a right-rear home and left-front origin; the operation page gives a top-left software origin. These different source states do not establish one installed coordinate configuration.

    The upgrade notes report an ACnode relay that de-powers the Smoothieboard, while the repository says it cuts +5 V. Relay terminals, ratings and safety-chain topology are undocumented. The config documents a RepRap Discount GLCD, but the wiki notes differ on panel state; neither confirms fitted wiring.

    The machine page lists a stock Reci Z2 tube, MYJG-80R supply, Leetro MPC6515C v2.0 controller and LaserCut 5.3. This historical Leetro reference remains separate from the Smoothieware/LightBurn configuration. No DB25 is evidenced for either controller variant.

    OLSK Large Laser

    Identity source: Appropedia lists Inmachines, a 1000 × 700 mm format, and a 75 W CO₂ laser. These are catalogue attributes, not proof of an individual machine’s installed configuration.

    V1 source and revision boundary

    The OLSK Large Laser V1 README identifies MKS-SBASE and grbl-LPC, while its linked firmware filename refers to grblHAL Teensy4. Separately, the OLSK Electronics repository names Laser Controller Shield V1.0 for Large Laser V1 and Small Laser V2. The V1 shield schematic is dated 2022-09-19 and depicts Teensy 4.1, ATtiny45, relay, CN1/CN2 motor-control headers, CN3 laser interface, two three-position STOP sensor headers and a 12 V power connector. It is a separate design reference: the sources do not prove that this shield is fitted to the unit in the Board2022 wiring sheet or resolve the MKS/Teensy conflict.

    Contact inventory and wiring status

    The visible SmoothieBox diagram lists 106 positions across 21 machine-side reference groups from the V1 machine wiring sheet and shield schematic. Printed driver, PSU, sensor, plug and shield positions are identified individually. Unnumbered or functionless marks are explicitly labelled as editorial drawing positions or unknown leads. All 106 are OPEN in this revision; it claims no fitted cable, electrical compatibility, DB25, or wiring approval. Mains, laser high-voltage, fire/enable and water-protection interfaces remain outside candidate routes.

    Visual transcription correction

    The fan-equipped nine-terminal V± supply is drawn separately from the far-right laser PSU; its output voltage and rating are unprinted. The laser PSU has the separate six-terminal control and three-terminal mains blocks. The chiller drawing labels only leads 1 and 3; no contact 2 is transcribed. The unsupported six-position-plug entry has been withdrawn.

    The retained inventory contains 93 printed source-marked positions and 13 editorial lead/conductor references. The separate shield field connectors contribute 21 positions; its board-local ISP/test contacts are outside that subtotal. The remaining unnamed controller terminals and depicted component leads are not a reconciled physical contact map. CN1/CN2 are Teensy controller outputs, so no SmoothieBox STEP/DIR output is routed to them. All 106 positions remain OPEN with zero guesses.
